A hefty gold coin. A one-of-a-kind jeweler's work: the embossed bitcoin symbol on the obverse is crafted with such detail that microscopic anti-counterfeiting engravings are visible. On the reverse — a QR code and a string of over sixty characters etched with a laser. The edge of the coin is a work of art in itself: a pattern of interwoven chains, and beneath a holographic seal lies a microchip with a private key. Whoever commissioned this clearly trusted neither exchanges, nor banks, nor even their own computer. Their entire fortune — in a single piece of gold you can hold in your hand. The coin itself as jewelry is worth a fortune, but what's stored on the chip inside is on a completely different scale.

A fairly heavy gold coin — a Tsarist chervonets. Darkened with age, but gold is gold — it doesn't rust and doesn't lose value. How such things end up in the Zone is an interesting question. Maybe one of the old-timers stashed it before the first Emission, or perhaps some black digger tried to carry it across the Perimeter and didn't make it. In any case, a trader will pay well for a gold coin — the metal is pure, without impurities.
